newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen hits new highs, upside seen limited.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen hits new highs, upside seen limited.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures reached new highs on Friday on continued confidence of a stable Japanese rate policy but dealers said there was limited upside potential.

"Dealers reckon there is no way the Bank of Japan will move rates up. That's why the market has been so strong. But the contracts are so strong it is difficult to imagine them going much higher," said one Singapore dealer with a European bank.
"I just don't think it can go any further," he said.
The lead June Euroyen contract stood at 99.28 in late trade after hitting a new contract high of 99.30 against an IMM close at 99.27.
Another dealer said the June Euroyen contract faced stiff resistance above 99.30. If it broke 99.30 it would encounter another barrier at around 99.33, he said.
Dealers said part of the early strength in Euroyen came from a rise in the Japanese government bond (JGB) futures but Euroyen then hit a bout of profit-taking.
December JGBs closed at a fresh contract high of 124.75 against an opening 124.50.

Dealers said the bullish tone of JGB futures was due in part to Thursday's news that the Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau would maintain its portfolio strategy, which is heavily weighted towards government bonds.

Sentiment was also boosted by indications of slowing economic growth and expectations a Liberal Democratic Party-led coalition would hike Japan's consumption tax and introduce a supplementary budget after last Sunday's election.
Eurodollar futures were almost unchanged after overnight U.S. treasuries weakened on the back of a sharp drop in U.S. weekly jobless claims data.
March and June Eurodollars closed at 94.30 and 94.14 respectively against their IMM settlements at 94.29 and 94.14.
Turnover for both months was under 7,500 lots.
